transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-17 10:00 PST | Duration 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Rajiv Singh (AstraHealth Head of Platform), Lena Ortiz (AstraHealth DevOps), Marcus Lee (AstraHealth ML Eng), Priya Nair (AstraHealth Security)

Summary: quick status on networking and routing, review of this week's benchmark results, tuning suggestions for batching/kv cache, plan for canary upgrade to model v2, outstanding security questions around KMS and audit logs.

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving time, quick roll call?
00:05 Rajiv (AstraHealth): Rajiv here, Lena, Marcus, Priya on the call too. thanks Alex.
00:10 Alex (Redwood AE): great. Maya, want to kick off with the results from the test harness you ran yesterday?
00:18 Maya (Redwood SE): yeah sure. um, we ran the 500-request burst and also the steady 200rps for 10 minutes on the staging VPC. baseline numbers — p95 latency for the small prompt set is about 220ms when using the cached prefixes and our current batching config. without cache it jumps to ~870ms on the same machines, so the prefix caching is doing the heavy lifting. note, some of the transcripts in the harness show tokenization differences, so ignore the tiny variation.
00:45 Marcus (AstraHealth): when you say cached prefixes, that's the prefix/KV cache you mentioned in the docs? sometimes we saw stale responses, like older context bleeding, any idea if that's our integration or the runtime?
00:58 Maya (Redwood SE): good callout — likely integration. We saw a chance where the SDK wasn't clearing per-session KV on test job resets; we pushed a small client fix yesterday. config change will be in the repo under /infra/pilot/client-fix-20251216.
01:15 Lena (AstraHealth): I pulled the logs, there's also a few 502s during the burst window around 15:12, looks like egress timeouts to the control plane? We had our network team change MTU last week so not sure if it collides.
01:30 Alex (Redwood AE): that matches what we saw. Maya, can you explain the control plane interactions? customer is Private deployment in their VPC so control plane talk is minimal but there is still the optional telemetry egress, right?
01:45 Maya (Redwood SE): correct, so Redwood Private keeps the serving plane in your VPC, but the control plane does health checks and optional telemetry over TLS. we've provided a list of FQDNs and ports for egress; if you block them you can switch to full air-gap mode but you'll lose auto-updates and telemetry. the 502 cluster during the burst looked like an intermittent TLS handshake issue with the telemetry endpoint — could be an ephemeral route flapping.
02:10 Rajiv (AstraHealth): we prefer telemetry but need to keep it over the peered link — I'll have our network team validate the peering doesn't NAT the certificates. Lena, can you confirm?
02:20 Lena (AstraHealth): will do, I'll snapshot the firewall rules and send. but quick Q: if we flip to air-gap, how do we get control plane patches? do we need to schedule on-prem maintenance windows?
02:32 Maya (Redwood SE): yes, air-gap requires manual patch bundles. we provide signed update artifacts and instructions; it's a slower path but fully isolated. for pilot we'd recommend keeping telemetry but locking egress to the specific Redwood endpoints.
02:50 Marcus (AstraHealth): switching gear — what about the routing between model variants? we tried routing to the faster quantized variant and saw cost savings but the outputs sometimes changed in ways our NLU tests flagged.
03:05 Maya (Redwood SE): that's expected tradeoff. quantized fp16/int8 can introduce minor distributional changes. we recommend a couple approaches: 1) run A/B with small sample traffic and evals tied to your prompt set; 2) use canary routing with automatic fallback to the full-precision model on high-confidence mismatches; 3) apply partial quantization only on tails where latency matters. we actually have a policy snippet we'll send that implements fallback on low-confidence.
03:35 Alex (Redwood AE): Marcus, you mentioned NLU tests flagged diffs — can you share a concrete example?
03:40 Marcus (AstraHealth): yeah, on the medication extraction prompt the quantized variant missed a small entity twice. sample attached in the ticket. wasn't frequent but enough to concern QA.
03:50 Maya (Redwood SE): we'll look; sometimes tokenization and casing cause this. also ensure your ridge scoring threshold in the reranker isn't too tight. quick fix could be to route extraction tasks to full-precision and use quantized for summarization.
04:05 Priya (AstraHealth): quick security question — KMS integration. we're using AWS CMKs and want to ensure model cache encryption at rest and in transit to HSM? what does Redwood support on Private?
04:20 Maya (Redwood SE): Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS for both request logs and model cache snapshots. the runtime can encrypt KV cache and checkpoints using your CMK. HSM integrations are on the roadmap for this quarter; for now we use envelope encryption with your CMK. detailed spec in the security pack link we'll share.
04:45 Rajiv (AstraHealth): that helps. also need SOC 2 type II evidence — do you have recent reports?
04:52 Alex (Redwood AE): yes, we have SOC 2 and ISO docs in the vendor pack, will send the latest. Priya, we'll also add the audit log retention options we discussed.
05:10 Lena (AstraHealth): back to networking: our peering seems fine but we had intermittent latency spikes from 700ms to 1500ms in the midnight window. could that be autoscaling jitter?
05:25 Maya (Redwood SE): possible — autoscaling of GPU nodes can add cold-start latencies if a new replica is spun up. for the pilot we recommended reserved warm pool with instant burst capacity to avoid that. you can configure min nodes per pool or a burst bucket. we saw the midnight scale event corresponds with a cron job you mentioned earlier?
05:45 Rajiv (AstraHealth): yeah that's nightly ETL. we can schedule less intense tests during off-peak but for SLOs we need to account for that noise.
05:55 Alex (Redwood AE): operationally we can shave cold start out by bumping min replicas on the dedicated pool for the pilot, cost vs latency tradeoff — we ran numbers in the pricing sheet.
06:10 Marcus (AstraHealth): speaking of pricing, curious about committed capacity if we move from pilot to dedicated. is there a mid-size tier?
06:20 Alex (Redwood AE): yes we have quarterly reserved blocks and annuals. for pilot-to-prod many customers do a 3-month commit as a ramp. I'll post the exact tiers after the call.
06:30 Maya (Redwood SE): quick note on the harness — we noticed a small memory leak in the inference process under the heavy 10-minute run; it doesn't crash but grows 350MB over 10 minutes on the current image. we have a patch that reduces retention in the KV manager; will push to the pilot image later today.
06:50 Lena (AstraHealth): good to know, please tag the image so we can pin to staging. last time we had a mismatch between image tags and the deploy script.
07:00 Maya (Redwood SE): will do. image tag is pilot-20251217-kvfix. we'll update the helm values in the repo.
07:10 Rajiv (AstraHealth): on canary scheduling — we want to do a canary for model v2 but only if latency stays under 300ms p95. what's realistic?
07:22 Maya (Redwood SE): with the tuned batching and the kv fixes we believe p95 sub-300ms is achievable for your short prompts on 4xA10G pool. longer prompts will be higher; for the canary we'd route 5% traffic and run evals; automatic fallback kicks in if error rate or mismatch exceeds threshold.
07:45 Marcus (AstraHealth): how do rollbacks happen? is it automatic or manual? we've had bad experiences with automatic rollbacks that didn't capture silent quality regressions.
07:58 Maya (Redwood SE): both. the default is canary with automatic rollback on explicit criteria (latency, 5xx rate). content/regression checks need explicit eval hooks; we suggest manual approval for content-sensitive routes like extraction.
08:15 Priya (AstraHealth): audit logs question — retention and who can access? we need at least 1 year retention and SSO integration for RBAC.
08:25 Alex (Redwood AE): we support 1y retention as an add-on and SSO with SAML/SCIM for RBAC. we'll add a note to the security pack for Priya about the retention cost profile.
08:40 Maya (Redwood SE): small operational checklist for next week: confirm peering and firewall rules, pin new image tag, run 1k-request benchmark overnight, and start canary staging after we get benchmark numbers.
08:58 Rajiv (AstraHealth): sounds good. Marcus will lead the benchmark run and Lena will handle peering details.
09:05 Alex (Redwood AE): perfect. any other questions?
09:10 Lena (AstraHealth): one last thing — do you have a recommended config for batch size vs tail latency? we saw increasing batch to 256 improved throughput but pushed tail latency up.
09:22 Maya (Redwood SE): yes, tradeoff chart: lower batch sizes reduce p95 but increase cost per token; we recommend adaptive batching: target batch of 64 with max 128 and a fast-path for low-latency routes (batch size 8-16). I'll share the chart and a sample helm snippet.
09:44 Marcus (AstraHealth): thanks, also please include the sample eval script so we can reproduce the NLU checks.
09:50 Alex (Redwood AE): noted. we'll send links: pilot dashboard, security pack, patched image tag, updated pricing.
09:58 Rajiv (AstraHealth): ok thanks everyone. recap and we'll follow up via the ticketing thread.
10:05 Alex (Redwood AE): thanks, meeting adjourned.
